request.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Make a SMALL, TARGETED revision to the attached image. Output one 1024x1024 transparent RGBA source image, same top-down viewpoint.

The user asks for one correction: NO ARC FRAGMENTS MAY OVERLAP OR COVER ONE ANOTHER. Preserve the current overall circular perimeter arrangement, nearby inner/outer broken layers, offset gaps between the two layers, varied shapes and sizes, icy cyan / antique gold / small dark mauve accents, hand-painted ink-outline style, outer footprint and completely empty transparent center. Do not redesign the composition or increase the size or density of the pieces.

Separate all distinct arc fragments with clearly visible TRANSPARENT AIR. Their silhouettes must never cross, touch, cover, weave over/under, or merge. This applies to small fragments too. Two layers may alternate and nest alongside each other's gaps, but never overlap. Interaction is now conveyed ONLY by proximity, curved tips pointing past neighbors and staggered positions, not physical intersection. Leave at least 8 to 12 pixels of clear transparent space between the nearest edges of neighboring independent fragments at this resolution, including every pointed tip. A forked double tail belonging to one single arc is fine; two separate arcs crossing is not.

Inspect the whole image and resolve every collision. Specific obvious collisions to fix: the cyan sweep crossing the large gold crescent at the bottom around 6 o'clock; the tiny cyan fragment crossing the gold arc on the right around 3:30; the gold and cyan pair on the upper left around 10:30; the gold fragment touching or covering the cyan hook on the lower right around 5 o'clock. Also separate any other touching outlines, including the small cyan fragment near the long cyan arc at lower left. Move a fragment slightly along its row, shift it a little inward/outward, or shorten a pointed tip just enough to clear its neighbor. Keep each fragment's original silhouette identity as closely as possible. Do not solve collisions by deleting one of the two main arc shapes or filling a gap with a new huge blade.

Keep the effect on the OUTER CIRCULAR PERIMETER, with two close, incomplete neighboring rows and a large open center. Keep the larger gaps in one row offset from those of the other. Maintain natural variations of length, hook shape, forks, sharp notches and spacing; do not regularize into identical leaves or equal angular intervals. No extra rings, particles, diamonds, symbols, letters, crystals, floor, furnace, characters, labels or shadows. NO glow, smoky aura or translucent painted disk. True transparent background everywhere other than the arc strokes. No cropped strokes. Preserve the same crisp tapered charcoal ink lines, cyan/gold painted planes and restrained pale highlights.
